subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should later global `tools.exec` security policy override persisted per-session `/exec` defaults, and what reset or migration should apply to existing session entries?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests intentionally treat `/exec` as persisted session state, but the report shows that this can shadow stricter operator security config; automation cannot choose that security and compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Make global security policy win
options.body: Change precedence or add config-versioned reset semantics so stricter operator `tools.exec` policy invalidates or overrides stored session exec defaults, with migration/doctor coverage for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep current session persistence
options.body: Keep `/exec` as the stronger documented per-session default and add clearer diagnostics/reset commands so operators can find and clear session-local exec policy.

options.title: Add opt-in strict mode
options.body: Preserve current defaults but add an explicit strict global-policy mode that ignores or clears persisted `/exec` fields when operators need centralized enforcement.

recommendation.title: Make global security policy win
recommendation.body: Change precedence or add config-versioned reset semantics so stricter operator `tools.exec` policy invalidates or overrides stored session exec defaults, with migration/doctor coverage for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant `/exec` persistence and resolver behavior appears to originate in commits authored by this owner, and the policy spans docs, tests, and session-state semantics.
